newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Rice sold at 200 times global price in N.Korea - report.
newsitem.headline: Rice sold at 200 times global price in N.Korea - report.

text.p: Rice is traded at more than 200 times the international price in flood-hit North Korea, indicating a severe food shortage in the reclusive Stalinist state, a South Korean state agency said on Monday.
A report by the National Statistical Office said rice was sold at 38,400 won ($46.4) per kg (2.2 lbs) in North Korean black markets last May.
The price, the latest figure available, compared with 183 won per kg on international markets, Seoul officials said.

"There are wide gaps between officially-set consumer prices and black market prices in North Korea because of shortages of consumer goods, but differences are enormous for food, particularly rice," the report said.
Red Cross officials have said North Korea faces a long-term problem in feeding itself after floods and heavy rains this year and last year destroyed part of its arable land.

The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) launched a new 13 million Swiss franc ($10.3 million) programme last month in the communist country to feed 139,000 flood victims.

The North Korean government estimates this year's harvest would be two million tonnes short of target -- a shortfall of 40 percent of the grain needed to feed the 26 million population through 1997, according to Red Cross officials.
Devastating floods following torrential rain in August and September of 1995 led the secretive state to open up to outside aid agencies, including the IFRC and the Rome-based World Food Programme.

Houses, roads, factories and grain stores in the west and north-west of the country were swept away by floods, which also caused electricity shortages, aid agencies said. Ricefields were covered with mud and rubble.

After months of relief efforts, during which emerged widespread reports of near starvation in some areas and severe malnutrition in many regions, rains this year struck again, destroying bridges and irrigation works.
The National Statistical Office in South Korea said North Korea's devastated economy contracted an average of 4.5 percent annually for six years until last year.
North Korea's per capita income stood at $957 in 1995 against South Korea's $10,076, it said.
